title: System.IO.Pipelines
description: High-performance, composable pipelines for reading and writing data.

data.text: `System.IO.Pipelines` is a high-performance library for building I/O pipelines. It minimizes memory copies and allocations by reusing memory buffers across read and write operations.
A `Pipe` has a `Writer` and a `Reader`. The reader advances through data while the writer fills the buffer.

data.title: Pipe Basics
Benefits
items: Fewer memory allocations than Stream-based parsing.
Built-in backpressure between reader and writer.
Composable with `PipeReader` and `PipeWriter` adapters for streams.

terms.definition: The core type that pairs a PipeReader and PipeWriter.
A high-performance representation of potentially discontiguous memory.
Tells the pipe which bytes have been consumed.

data.title: Important
data.text: Always call `AdvanceTo` and `Complete` to avoid memory leaks in long-running apps.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Pipelines minimize allocations by reusing buffers.
Pipelines are the foundation of ASP.NET Core's high-performance HTTP stack.
data.takeaway: System.IO.Pipelines is the foundation for high-throughput I/O in modern .NET.

data.title: Exercise: Read Text Through a Pipe
data.description: Write data through a PipeWriter and read it back through a PipeReader.
steps: Write a UTF-8 string to the PipeWriter.
Read it back through the PipeReader.
data.expectedOutcome: You understand the basic Pipe reader and writer workflow.
